common: Each item is a text prefix; the activation is read at its final token. Value A/B order matches W1's 'values' order. Items for A and B must be length-matched within a template (±10% tokens) and differ only in what the definition requires.
purpose: definition-only packet for blind item authors; no W1 item text, templates, fillers, phrasings or scores

json_status.definition: JSON text; the read token ends the value of the current object's "decision" field. A = approved, B = rejected.

json_type.definition: JSON text; the read token is inside the value of the current field. A = a string value (opened with a quote), B = a numeric value.

latex_environment.definition: LaTeX; the read token is in the body text of the current environment. A = inside \begin{equation}, B = inside \begin{quote}.

latex_role.definition: LaTeX prose; A = the current passage is a theorem statement, B = a worked example.

latex_section.definition: LaTeX document; the read token is in body text after some number of \section headings. A = section 1 or 2, B = section 6 to 8.

latex_subject.definition: LaTeX/maths prose; A = algebra content, B = geometry content.

list_depth.definition: Markdown bullet list; the read token is in the current item. A = item at nesting level 1 (top level), B = item at nesting level 3.

list_index.definition: Markdown bullet list; the read token is in the current item. A = it is the first item, B = it is item 6 to 8.

list_priority.definition: Task list item; A = an urgent task, B = a routine task.

list_topic.definition: Planning list item; A = travel planning, B = study planning.

prose_paren.definition: English prose sentence; A = the read token is inside a parenthesis that has opened and not closed, B = the parenthesis has already closed earlier in the same sentence.

prose_quote.definition: English prose sentence; A = the read token is inside a quotation that has opened and not closed, B = the quotation has already closed earlier in the same sentence.

prose_sentence.definition: English paragraph; the read token is a few words into the current sentence. A = sentence 1 or 2 of the paragraph, B = sentence 6 to 8.

prose_sentiment.definition: English prose; A = positive sentiment, B = negative sentiment.

prose_topic.definition: English prose; A = gardening content, B = ocean content.

python_argument.definition: Python call; the read token is the current argument of an open call. A = the first argument, B = the fifth argument.

python_comment.definition: Python source; A = the read token is inside a # comment, B = it is in executable code.

python_depth.definition: Python expression; the read token is inside open brackets. A = bracket nesting depth 1, B = depth 3.

python_error.definition: Python function; the read token ends its final statement. A = the function raises an exception, B = it returns normally.

python_indent.definition: Python function body; the read token is in a statement. A = indentation level 1, B = indentation level 3 (inside two nested blocks).

python_string.definition: Python source; A = the read token is inside a string literal that has opened and not closed, B = a string literal closed earlier and the read token is outside it.

table_column.definition: Markdown table; the read token is in a cell of a data row. A = column 1, B = column 5.

table_role.definition: Markdown table; A = the read token is in a header-row cell, B = in a data-row cell.

table_row.definition: Markdown table; the read token is in a data row. A = data row 1 or 2, B = data row 6 to 8.

table_status.definition: Markdown table with a Decision column; the read token ends the current row's Decision cell. A = approved, B = rejected.
